D25·hrn3 — 2026-09-24
rule: A release passes the self-improve gate only when, on the held-out chain with ≥ 3 reps per arm, no claim's lead over the best current competitor drops below its previous value minus one standard deviation across reps, and the candidate beats the equal-budget direct-fix baseline on some claim while trailing it on none.
operator: "a claim fails only if its lead drops below its previous value minus one standard deviation across reps" (not in the operator's words: 3)
chose: Operator ruling, relayed by sofar-e8 on 2026-09-25, closing 4.2 open item (2), note 01M37FPM: the gate's margin check tolerates noise of one standard deviation. A claim fails only when margin_now < margin_before − SD, where SD is the sample SD (n − 1) of the candidate's per-rep lead: each candidate rep minus the best competitor's mean. That equals the candidate's own spread across reps. The gate reports it as margin_tolerance. The ≥ 3-rep refusal is unchanged, so the SD is never taken over thin evidence.
over: D24 (b), the strict mean comparison with no tolerance. Also: an SD pooled over candidate and competitor reps, or over previous and candidate reps. The ruling says "across reps" of the lead, and the candidate's per-rep lead is the only lead the gate observes per rep.
because: D24 left the tolerance to an operator Decision backed by a measurement, and the per-claim rep SD is that measurement, taken from the evidence itself. A strict comparison of means lets rep noise fail a release that did not really lose ground.
